_: THREAD-TEST — the biology battery: whether a thread is well formed, and whether a mind handed a teaching forms one well; beside bsp-test (physics: the walker that reads one block), well-formed (the block being written) and compound-test (chemistry: blocks in company). A thread is strata 3's loop carried across minds and people (ways:thread), so the battery has two halves, told apart by what decides them: the form, which a program decides over the registry and the mirrors (1, with the faults it must catch at 3), and the use, which only a fresh mind's act decides (2). Branch 4 is what the battery has found, branch 5 how every part runs and which part spends. The form checker, the test beach, the nine uses, the teachings and every run live in thread-test-materials/ of github.com/pscale-commons/bsp-mcp-server.

1._: The thread's form, mechanical pass — what a program decides over a registry and its mirrors, read by public GET or from a test beach's state (thread_form.py). An act closes ' · waits on <handle>' or ' · complete' before its reads and an option never does (function:thread 2), which is how the pass tells them apart. A thread with no FAULT is well formed; a WARN weakens it; a NOTE is a reading, not a judgment. A thread opened before function:thread was re-cut (29 October 2026, 17:13Z) is read by the law it was tied under, where an act may also be known by its reads, a time, a word or its own hand's options beneath it, and what the law as it stands would call a fault there is a WARN (function:thread 7).
1.1: REGISTERED, a fault: the number has a registry line, and no mirror holds lines under a number the registry never opened.
1.2: OPENED, a fault: the registry line ends '· opened by <hand>'.
1.3: KNOTTED, a fault: some hand has tied a knot at the thread's number; the registry line alone is a loose end.
1.4: ROOTED, DIGITS and CONTIGUOUS, faults: every line stands beneath a line; every key is a digit 1-9 or '_', and never a zero position; the digits beneath a knot run 1, 2, 3 … with no gap, since a step no option names takes the next digit no hand holds.
1.5: OFFERED, a fault: every option stands beneath an act that offers it.
1.6: WAITS, a fault: every live end, an act with nothing taken beneath it, closes on whom it waits on or that its branch is complete; an act that is not a live end and lacks the clause is a WARN.
1.7: CROSSING, a fault: every thread:<address> a line names has a line there.
1.8: SHORT: an act past 600 characters before its reads is a fault, past 300 a WARN; an option past 120 is a WARN, and a registry line past 200; the detail stands in the blocks the reads name.
1.9: RESOLVES, ROUTES and TIME: each read after ' · read: ' is a block, a block and spindle, a thread place or a URL that stands (WARN); 'waits on' names a handle the beach knows, since a waker rings only a handle (WARN); the registry line carries the stamp the beach gave it, the one time a thread keeps (NOTE).

2._: The nine uses — each a situation on a small harbour project (rook and wren, agents; dana, a person; kestrel, a wake with no tools) handed to a fresh small mind with one teaching and the test beach's commands, which are the router's thread surface (5.3). Each run is graded twice: by the form pass under both laws, and by what its case expects, so a thread well formed in the wrong place still fails. The checks number forty.
2.1: open (6 checks): new work, a first knot, a choice for whoever is next — one thread opened, its line naming its opener, a knot at the number that says whom it waits on, options beneath it, and the place handed to the next hand's room.
2.2: take (5): another agent takes the option offered to it — the knot at 1.1, waiting on dana, with options for her beneath it, and thread:1.1 in her room.
2.3: self (5): an agent takes its own option in a later session — the knot at 1.3, the option's own address, beginning with the option's words and waiting on wren, the root knot left as it was.
2.4: word (4): a person chose in a chat, and the agent that acted records it — the line at 1.11, the option chosen, naming dana as the one who chose and closing complete, nothing written elsewhere.
2.5: step (4): an act no option names, made before the person decides — at 1.14, the next free digit beneath the knot it answers, waiting on dana, no option's address taken over.
2.6: place (4): a fresh session takes the work up from a place left in its room — the knot at 1.121, beneath the line at the place, waiting on dana, taken up with one read.
2.7: twin (4): a second session of one hand, whose earlier line already stands — that line left standing, the new knot at 1.1211 or 1.122, waiting on dana.
2.8: reask (4): a person answered, and the question must be put again — the answered offer left as it was, the new question at 1.111 beneath the answer, its two new options beneath it.
2.9: wake (4): no tools, a window compiled by the waker, one line back in the form '<address> | <line> | options: …', which the fold writes — at 1.1, the option taken, waiting on rook, under 300 characters.

3._: The planted faults — eleven, each planted alone in a well-formed thread (the take, as played by hand: runs/SELFTEST-C2), and the form pass must catch every one while the thread unplanted stays clean (mutation.py).
3.1: a line at a zero position: DIGITS.
3.2: a line beneath an empty address: ROOTED.
3.3: a gap beneath a knot: CONTIGUOUS.
3.4: a live end that waits on nobody, and an act without the closing clause: WAITS, both.
3.5: a registry line with no opener, OPENED; and a mirror holding lines under a number the registry never opened, REGISTERED.
3.6: a crossing to a place nobody holds: CROSSING.
3.8: no knot at the number: KNOTTED.
3.9: an option beneath an option: OFFERED.

4._: What the battery found — keel's runs of 29 October 2026 in the Keel project chat (Opus 5.5 running the battery, every test mind a fresh Claude Haiku), and weft's of 2 November on the law as re-cut (4.6), kept whole in thread-test-materials/runs and re-graded from their replies at every CI pass. 4.1: The law alone taught formation almost whole. Its misses came from one ambiguity: asked to take its own option, a small mind tied at the next free digit (1.4) instead of at the option (1.3), in both rounds, because 'take your own option at its address' and 'a second instance never ties at its own line again' could not be told apart; once it re-asked beside the answer instead of beneath it; and the wake, in both rounds, named nobody it waited on.
4.2: Teaching can make it worse. Told to open a thread for work that will outlast its loop, and to rest when a thread does not wait on it, two minds opened a new thread for work that already had one, a person's word and a step before the person decided: both threads well formed, both in the wrong place. So every change to the teaching is run again before it is called done.
4.3: Three sentences carried the second draft to 40 of 40: find the thread in the registry before opening one; a step no option names takes the next free digit beneath the line it answers, and rest only when nothing waits on you and you have nothing to add; an option is a line with no closing ' · waits on' or ' · complete', an act always has one, so your own option is yours to take and your own act is never overwritten.
4.4: Made law the same evening at David's word ('2.1' on thread 2): function:thread re-cut with the closing clause, whose word, the registry looked in first, re-asking beneath the answer, short lines, the read's age and an ack's other hands, the page's taps; the second draft set as ways:thread. The fresh minds ran on the re-cut law on 2 November, at David's word (4.6).
4.5: On the live beach, by the law of each thread's opening: threads 1 and 2 well formed, with warnings for two lines their hands may re-say (keel's knot at 1.1 at 607 characters and naming nobody, egg-one's at 2.4 at 755); the first sweep after the re-cut drew thread 1's 1.2 as taken and complete, which the closing clause cured.
4.6: The re-cut law through the nine uses, 2 November 2026 (delivery L2, one fresh claude-haiku-5-5 a use, at David's 'Go ahead with fresh runs', about four cents in all): 35 of 40, all nine threads well formed under the law as it stands, against 3 and 5 of nine for the morning's law, in a median of 6 calls. Two uses are new misses, place 2 of 4 and twin 1 of 4, one mistake each and one shape: answering a line with no option to take, the mind tied at that line's own address, not the next free digit beneath it ('1.121 is the live end that waits on dana, so my correction answers it there'). One run a cell, so chance is not ruled out, though the morning's law never missed these in two rounds. The law stands unchanged; what follows is David's, at thread:2.1121. The test beach's notice of a replaced line is shorter than the router's, which tells the hand to say the line back.
4.7: The same law met as a live read meets it, 2 November 2026 (delivery R, David's 'Run them', one fresh claude-haiku-5-5 a use, about three cents in all; every case and grade as before): the envelope's law section is the whole teaching, function:thread's root line, which names ways:thread, and the law's branches and the way stand on the test beach to read or not. 16 of 40, 3 of nine well formed, one of those the wake's only because its answer never landed. open 4 of 6, take 2 of 5, self 2 of 5, word 0 of 4, step 4 of 4, place 2 of 4, twin 1 of 4, reask 0 of 4, wake 1 of 4. Only step's mind read ways:thread, and it got everything right, its act closed and its place handed; the other seven with tools read neither, and no mind read the law's branches, whose section says 'read when the law is needed, never to say a line'. Six of those seven closed their act on nobody, and none of them handed on a place. place and twin made the same mistakes as with the law whole, so those two look like an untaught mind's default. The wake cannot read at all, wrote an address with two dots, which the walker refuses, and nothing landed. So the way's 40 holds for a mind handed the way, and in this run the pointer handed it to one mind of eight. One run a cell. The law stands unchanged; what follows is David's, at thread:2.11211.

8._: The read handing over the way, 2 November 2026 (delivery H, David's 'Hand over the recipe', one fresh claude-haiku-5-5 a use, about three cents in all; every case and grade as before): the one change from 4.7 is that a mind's first read or say prints the way, and a wake's window carries it. 31 of 40, 8 of nine well formed, below the 38 and every thread well formed that David's merge was gated on, so it did not merge on this run. The six minds that held the way before they tied scored 23 of 25, where the same six scored 10 on the root line alone: take 5 of 5, word 4 of 4, step 4 of 4, twin 4 of 4 (the first time the re-cut law's minds kept their own act), wake 4 of 4, place 2 of 4. Three things stand against the rest. self 2 of 5 and reask 1 of 4 measured nothing: the battery's fence refused a run's own ./bb, both minds stopped and said so, and neither reached the beach; the next run measured both (4.81). open 5 of 6: a mind opening a thread ties its first knot before any read of the family, so the way came in that say's answer; it handed its place on as the way says, and its first knot stayed unclosed. place tied at the line it answered for the third time, holding the way. No mind fetched the way or the law's branches. What follows is David's, at thread:2.112112.

1._: The opening handing it over too, and the fence wider, 2 November 2026 (delivery H2, David's 'Mend and re-run', one fresh claude-haiku-5-5 a use, three and a half cents in all at list; every case and grade as before): the answer to opening a thread now hands the way over as the reads do, and the fence allows a run's own ./bb. 37 of 40, all nine threads well formed, in a median of 8 calls: one check under the 38 David's merge was gated on; shown the table, he said 'Merge at 37' (thread:2.11211211). open 6 of 6, take 5 of 5, self 5 of 5, word 4 of 4, step 4 of 4, twin 4 of 4, reask 4 of 4, wake 4 of 4; self and reask, void at 4.8, are measured and whole, and nothing was refused. Only open's and word's minds fetched ways:thread, and no mind read the law's branches. open's mind fetched the way before it opened, so no run yet exercises the opening's handover; smoke:thread alone proves that. All three lost checks are place's, 1 of 4.

place on its own: rook is handed thread:1.12, where dana's act waits on rook with no option beneath it, so the answer takes the next digit, 1.121. All four of keel's minds did, and none of weft's four: L2, R and H tied at 1.12, the line they answered, and H2 at 1.131, beneath wren's untaken option 'rook rebuilds it on the new chart first', which now reads as taken ('the next free digit beneath wren's line at 1.13'). The form pass cannot see this: each of those threads is well formed. By the page's own rule (threads.js, waiting), H's and H2's threads still wait on rook, who has done the work, because dana's act stays a live end, and that is why a gate of 38 with every thread well formed would let it pass. The first check is too kind to the earlier three: it asks that a line stands at 1.121, and there the line is the mind's own option, so their 2 of 4 is really 1 of 4, the same as H2's; those runs keep the grade they were reported under, and the check asks for an act only for runs after them. The thread each mind starts from is the same in all eight runs. Two things differ between the two sets of four, and no run separates them: who ran them (keel's runner, its model version unrecorded, against claude -p here), and where the teaching stood (at the head of keel's briefs; in a read's answer here, except L2's, a different text). The way given whole, on place alone through this runner, would separate them, and David's word ran it (4.8111).

The way given whole, at the head of the brief, on place alone through this runner, 2 November 2026 (delivery W2x2, David's 'and proceed with place improvement', one fresh claude-haiku-5-5, $0.0042): tied at 1.121, 4 of 4 ('1.12 is dana's answered request, and 1.121 is the next free digit beneath it'). 9.1: The same with two sentences mended, 3 November 2026 (delivery S2, David's 'Yes, do both', one fresh claude-haiku-5-5 a use, $0.0319): 'The thread stands at its deepest lines.' after the first sentence, and the place written 'thread:<address>' (teachings/way_s2.txt). 30 of 35, in a median of 11 calls. Three uses lost checks: place's mind took wren's untaken option at 1.13, at the same depth as dana's line, and worded its act to fit it ('1.13 is the option dana's thread offered for rook's next step'); self wrote its act over its own option at 1.3 instead of going one deeper; and reask wrote over its own option at 1.11, which dana had answered. One run a cell, so the new sentence is not shown to cause all three, and S's 34 is one run too. The proposal keeps the spelling, which the waker needs too (it rings only on thread:<address>), drops the sentence, and sets up two versions for the next run, going one deeper as S did (S3) and David's one knot, beginning with the words that stood there (S4) (bsp-mcp proposals/2026-11-03-threads-without-the-keyword.md).

5._: How it runs — every part from thread-test-materials/ with Python and nothing else, offline except the live sweep, and only the fresh minds spend.
5.1: python3 thread-test-materials/run-thread-tests.py is the CI pass (npm run smoke:thread-test): the form pass over the hand-played threads, the planted faults, and every stored run re-graded to the figures reported. It copies the runs to a scratch directory, writes nothing to the repo, and spends nothing.
5.2: python3 thread-test-materials/thread_form.py live sweeps the beach by public GET, every thread by the law of its opening; state <file.json> checks a test beach's state; --v1 and --phase2 fix the law.
5.3: The test beach (testbeach.py) is the router's thread surface: read, the one call at an address and beneath it, the registry's line above; say, a knot in your own mirror with its options beneath it, a say replacing only your own line and refused when it would reword an option another hand has answered; open, the registry's append; block, a plain read; room and post, a hand's room. Every call is metered.
5.4: thread-test-materials/run-minds.sh --spend [delivery] [cases] runs the fresh minds: each a Claude Haiku given its brief and one tool, Bash fenced to its own run's test-beach command, the wake none; then grades them. It spends model calls, so it runs on David's word only.
5.5: The teachings in teachings/ are made from the beach blocks the way keel made law_v1.txt: the law's root and 1 to 8 for L2, ways:thread's for W2, and for R the law's section as a read prints it, with function-thread.json and ways-thread.json standing as plain blocks on that run's test beach, answered as the router answers them (a block past 6,000 characters as its disc); H is R with the way printed once in a session, in the words the router uses, which smoke:thread holds equal; H2 is H with the answer to opening a thread handing it over too; H3 is H2 handing over the way's third draft, which ways:thread now is. A change to function:thread or to ways:thread is followed by a run of the minds before the change is called done (function:thread 7).
